findings.statement: All nine obligation records carry contract='uncontracted' and contract_basis='block-level SAFETY present but no # Safety fn contract'. The contract exists only in the boundary receipt, not at the interface or in the obligation record.

The boundary receipt openssh-v1l-sites.json is bound to candidate 8a54aba58f35dd62af5c78551169d0e8a9276469 (v1k, 2026-10-28), not to S=0238c6e4adbc7ed85a42be68b6fb965e139bd93e. The b76c closures accept it only through the operation-span content hash, which re-checks the operation text but not the callers the discharge cites.

The receipt's establishing witnesses no longer point at the code that establishes the preconditions: v3_prn i2v dispatch cited at 226-246/:279 is now at 308/:355; v3_conf v2i dispatch cited at 1029-1059 is now at 1111 (v3_prn.rs +907, v3_conf.rs +1236, v3_lib.rs +424 between the receipt's candidate and S); ui index loads cited at 277/447/500/525 are now at 282/452/503/528; the v3_san row table cited at 1211-1214 is now at 1232. The v3_akid row citation 203-218 still contains the row at 207, and the v3_san alt_row citation 1193-1217 still contains alt_row at 1207.

For OSSH-V1L-013/014/015 the boundary receipt declares :1163/:1174/:1184 while the reviewed items are at :1176/:1187/:1197. The closure's own scoped_discharge_attempt records covers_site=false for all three, yet sets DISCHARGED on the strength of span_hash==span_current_hash. Content binding is sound, but the recorded coordinate does not identify the site.

push_cstr_or_null (OSSH-V1L-009) has no `# Safety` fn contract; its block comment refers to a contract stated elsewhere. The receipt's established_by also names a second call path ('the `word` literal path') that does not exist: there is exactly one call site (eng_fat.rs:235).

receipt_identity.note: The closure receipts analyse the correct span source (0238c6e4a) but are generated from worktrees at later heads; the v1l boundary receipt predates S. Only the operation bodies are content-rebound. Regenerating the v1l receipt at S with current witnesses and re-running NC-04..NC-15 against the S binaries is required before any of these nine is cited as final evidence at S.

hidden_obligations: F09: push_cstr_or_null transfers a NUL-termination obligation to callers with no `# Safety` contract; the obligation is reported in contract_basis but not at the interface

does_not_prove: No runtime execution of the nine code paths was observed in this review. Compilation was forbidden by the §6.1 OOM gate (free -g: 17 GiB available; cap min(8, 17-16)=1g < 2g floor), and the receipt's NC-04..NC-15 binaries were not retained, so their recorded v1k results are NOT evidence for this review.

The controls are source-level structural instruments. They prove call-site/provenance/cast/row pairing and would fail on the seven mutated violation classes, but they cannot prove absence of aliasing UB, double release or a bad generic-evaluation path at run time.
No Miri, ASan, TSan or Tree Borrows run. No cryptographic or compatibility court was run; this is a safety/contract review only.

The external C ABI obligations (X509V3_EXT_print callers, X509V3_EXT_nconf ctx, UI_method_set_ex_data index writers, ENGINE_set_default_string def_list) are unchanged from the authority and are retained, not discharged, by this review.
The 56 openssh-v1i obligations were inventoried only, not reviewed; their contracts are also recorded as 'uncontracted' and the same evidence-identity questions apply to them.
The witnesses cited in the v1l boundary receipt are stale; ACCEPT verdicts here rest on source read during this review, not on that receipt.
